title: 1977 Ford Bronco
description: The first-generation 1977 Ford Bronco Ranger remains one of the most desired classics, known for its enduring value and enjoyable driving experience. This stunning example was uniquely ordered by a dealer principal with an array of rarely seen features including the Ranger Package, stripe delete, skid plates, power steering, black sidewall tires, “Northland Special Package,” remote and chrome mirrors, locking gas caps, power brakes, rocker panel moldings, rear seat, manual AM radio, free running front hubs, extra cooling radiator, convenience group, heavy-duty shocks, and front stabilizer bar. This specific combination of paint codes and options makes it a rare 1 of 51 produced that year. It fires up with ease, offering a truly impressive and ready-to-drive experience, with functioning heat, AM radio, power steering, power brakes, gauges, and lights. The exterior displays a natural patina, enhancing its vintage appeal. Recent enhancements include a new battery, tuned carburetor, and a fresh carpet kit. This Bronco is a blast to drive, guaranteed to turn heads and put a smile on your face. It comes complete with its Deluxe Marti Report, original locking fuel caps, a clean title, and newer tires, representing a smart acquisition for any enthusiast.

title: 1972 Datsun 240Z
description: This extraordinary 1972 Datsun 240Z, a timeless classic and pioneer of Japanese sports cars, has been meticulously preserved and maintained to its original glory. Its sleek, iconic lines and fresh Silver/White paintwork evoke an era of simplicity and elegance, complemented by brilliantly shining paint, well-preserved chrome bumpers, and distinctive round headlamps. Powering this authentic beauty is a spirited inline-six-cylinder engine, delivering a perfect balance of power and precision. The smooth-shifting manual transmission provides complete control, inviting an engaging driving experience on the open road.

title: 1970 Pontiac GTO
description: This stunning 1970 Pontiac GTO Judge, finished in its unmistakable Orbit Orange with bold Judge decals, is one of the most iconic muscle cars of its era. The Judge was Pontiac's high-performance statement, loud in both style and power, with its bright orange paint, black accents, chrome bumpers, signature rear spoiler, hood-mounted tachometer, and factory PMD wheels wrapped in Firestone Wide Oval tires. Powering this legend is the formidable 400ci L74 V8, rated at 366 horsepower and equipped with the famous Ram Air induction system. A four-speed manual transmission paired with a Hurst shifter provides a direct connection to the driver, complemented by upgraded springs and shocks for enhanced ride and handling, and a dual exhaust that amplifies its engine's growl. The cabin exudes classic muscle car charm with black leather bucket seats, a wooden steering wheel, and a rally gauge cluster, along with an added Bosch temperature and fuel gauge for accuracy. Period features like an AM radio, ceiling-mounted seat belt storage, crank windows, air conditioning, and heat maintain a simple yet functional interior. This GTO Judge stands as a highly collectible piece of American automotive history, capturing the spirit of being bold, fast, and commanding attention.

title: 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle
description:
This stunning 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle SS is a prime example of what many consider the ultimate muscle car. Under the hood lies a powerful non-numbers matching 1970 454 V8 engine, mated to a Muncie 4-speed manual transmission. The engine was rebuilt approximately 10,000 miles ago, featuring forged pistons, Eagle rods, Total Rollerz, and bored 30 over, all within a body that still proudly wears its original Forest Green exterior paint. Performance enhancements include a Holly 850 Duel pumper carb, Chrome Edelbrock highrise intake manifold, Hooker headers, a full 3-inch exhaust with electric cutouts, MSD Ignition, front disc brakes, and a 3.55 rear gear. This classic rides on 5-spoke Crager wheels wrapped in new BFGoodrich tires.

The Chevelle, a mid-size model introduced in 1964, saw its second generation become arguably the most popular, distinguished by its distinctly sculpted “coke bottle” body with tapered fenders and a rear quarter kick-up. The 1970 model year brought a squared-up front fascia and revised options, with the potent 454ci V8 in the SS being the most powerful engine choice. The quad headlights remain a well-regarded Chevelle feature, often associated with higher value.

title: 1969 Dodge Charger
description: This iconic 1969 Dodge Charger R/T presents with a sleek black exterior complemented by a clean black interior. Powering this classic muscle car is a robust 383ci V8 engine, delivering an impressive 485hp, paired with a responsive 4-speed manual transmission. Enhancing both performance and driving experience, this Charger features power steering, power brakes with front discs, an aftermarket tachometer, and a Hurst shifter. Key performance upgrades include an MSD Distributor, K&N air filter, Demor carburetors, Edelbrock intake, and Mopar Performance heads. The aggressive stance is completed with American Racing wheels. The 1969 Charger, built on the Chrysler B platform, is celebrated for its distinctive styling cues like the undivided grille, rounded taillights, and hidden headlights, a design that captivated buyers with over 96,000 units produced in its redesigned year.

title: 1969 Chevrolet Camaro
description: This iconic 1969 Chevrolet Camaro Z/28 boasts a powerful 454ci big block engine, paired with an automatic transmission, offering a smooth start and steady idle. Its stunning Dover White finish showcases straight body lines and a distinctive black hood stripe, with paint displaying exceptional depth. The vehicle has undergone a meticulous full nut and bolt rotisserie restoration, ensuring its spectacular condition. The interior features expertly hand-worked seats, fresh carpeting, and a well-preserved dashboard with new old stock gauges. The 1969 redesign, characterized by its longer, lower profile and detailed styling, remains a highly desired model for collectors and continues to influence modern automotive design.

title: 1967 Ford Mustang
description: This exceptional 1967 Ford Mustang Fastback has undergone a meticulous fifteen-year, frame-off restoration, resulting in a superb example of American muscle. Originally equipped with a 289ci engine and automatic transmission, this vehicle has been extensively upgraded to a powerful 302ci V8, paired with a responsive 4-speed manual transmission. The engine received a complete machining, bored .30 over, and fitted with a larger cam, hardened valves, seats, and a 550 Holley carburetor. Finished in a striking Jazz Blue, a departure from its original Dark Moss Green, this Fastback features a completely redone interior with new wiring and LED lighting. Performance enhancements include power steering, front disc brakes, and a 2.79 rear end. This iconic Fastback, renowned for its design and featuring a Sport Deck Rear seat, delivers a thrilling driving experience.

title: 1965 Chevrolet Corvette
description: The second generation of Corvette, produced from 1963 to 1967, is widely regarded as one of the finest. This era introduced iconic styling cues such as quad headlights, split taillights, a distinctive raised windsplit, and knock-off wheels. This stunning 1965 Corvette Stingray convertible is presented in a beautiful Marina Blue finish over a complementary blue interior, appearing neat and tidy throughout. Equipped with desirable features like power windows, striking side pipes, and classic whitewall tires, it embodies vintage American sports car appeal. Performance is delivered by a robust 350 hp 327 V8 engine that starts with enthusiasm, paired with a smooth-shifting 4-speed manual transmission, offering an exhilarating driving experience with excellent sound and braking.

title: 1969 Ford Mustang
description:
In 1969, the legendary Mach 1 nameplate debuted, marking Ford's formidable entry into one of Detroit's most fiercely competitive performance car markets. Amidst formidable contenders like the Boss 302, Boss 429, Shelby GT350, and Shelby GT500, the Mach 1 distinguished itself by dramatically outselling them all. Achieving an astounding 72,458 units in its inaugural year, nearly a quarter of all Mustang sales, its success was so profound that Ford retired the GT model, deeming it obsolete. This pristine example, presented in a radiant Candy Apple Red, commands attention with its bold black hood stripe, iconic Mach 1 side and rear badging, and prominent 351 hood badging, perfectly embodying the authentic first-year details that collectors covet.

Beneath the hood resides the powerful 351 cubic inch Windsor V8 engine, seamlessly paired with an automatic transmission. The 351 was strategically chosen as the standard engine for the Mach 1, offering a perfect blend of accessibility and uncompromised performance. It delivers the smooth, authoritative pull characteristic of a classic American V8, accompanied by an exhilarating and authentic exhaust note. The Mach 1's performance prowess was famously demonstrated at the Bonneville Salt Flats, where a modified version shattered 295 USAC land speed and endurance records, a testament Ford proudly highlighted in its advertising campaigns.

Step inside to an interior designed for both luxury and sport. Black leather seats provide a striking contrast against a rich wood dash and matching interior door panels, adorned with the distinctive Mach 1 logo. This sophisticated combination, standard on the Mach 1, offered an elevated cabin experience unmatched by lesser Mustangs. Further enhancing its character are a leather-wrapped steering wheel, a classic glove box clock, a functional Sunpro oil pressure gauge, and rear window vent covers. The exterior is completed with elegant pinstripes running along the sides and rear, a gleaming chrome front bumper, a black underlip, and stylish silver wheels, creating a cohesive and sharp aesthetic from every angle.

The 1969 Mach 1 perfectly captured the zeitgeist of its era, emerging at the pinnacle of the muscle car movement before impending emissions regulations and fuel crises reshaped the automotive landscape. First-year models in such exceptional condition and desirable colors are increasingly sought after by collectors, representing a rare opportunity to own a significant piece of American automotive history.

title: 1965 Pontiac GTO
description:
The 1965 Pontiac GTO Convertible, an enduring icon among muscle cars, combines potent performance with classic styling. Under the hood, a robust 389ci V8 engine delivers impressive power, channeled through a responsive 4-speed manual transmission. Performance has been enhanced with an Edelbrock intake manifold, further adorned with polished valve covers and an air cleaner.

Finished in a lustrous Starlight Black, the bodywork is straight and reflective, complemented by gleaming exterior chrome. The car maintains its authentic stance on 14-inch factory steel wheels, featuring correct beauty rings and hubcaps, fitted with BFGoodrich Radial T/A tires for excellent handling. The black interior, noted to have been refinished in 2017, remains in very good condition, presenting bucket seats with a center console, a Hurst T-Handle shifter, and a wood grain steering wheel. The white convertible top is in excellent condition, offering a sophisticated contrast. Additional features include power steering, power brakes, and a power top, enhancing the driving experience of this legendary "Muscle Car." This GTO is a fantastic example, ready to impress with its blend of power and classic appeal.

title: 1971 GMC C-1500
description: This 1971 C-1500 Longbed pickup stands in immaculate condition, presenting extremely well after an intense, total restoration where virtually every component was meticulously addressed, cleaned, painted, or replaced. Both the engine and transmission have been rebuilt, ensuring robust performance. Under the hood, the 396ci V8 engine features performance upgrades including headers, an Edelbrock intake, carburetor, and air cleaner, complemented by power steering and power brakes for a refined driving experience. Further enhancements include new shocks, air conditioning, Flowmaster mufflers, and a practical tonneau cover. The interior maintains its immaculate state, perfectly complementing the exterior's striking two-tone paint and excellent trim.

title: 1968 Dodge Charger
description: This second-generation 1968 Dodge Charger is a striking example, finished in a beautiful blue metallic that showcases well, complemented by chrome and brightwork in good condition. The interior is neat, tidy, and well-kept, featuring bucket seats. Under the hood, a healthy 383ci V8, paired with a rebuilt automatic transmission and a 3.55:1 rear end, has been significantly enhanced. Performance upgrades include a 400HP Edelbrock Performer kit, Hooker headers, Edelbrock heads, carburetor, and intake, all capped with a chrome air cleaner. The car benefits from a rebuilt front suspension and the addition of front disc brakes, ensuring improved handling. It rides on 16-inch wheels with BF Goodrich white letter radial tires, and an aggressive dual exhaust system delivers an awesome sound. This is a very solid vehicle, with dry and solid trunk and floor pans, offering a blast to drive for any enthusiast.

title: 1973 Dodge Challenger
description: The Dodge Challenger, a legendary nameplate in automotive history, established itself as a quintessential pony car during its first generation from 1969 to 1974. This particular 1973 Challenger perfectly embodies the era's classic styling, featuring a vibrant Bright Red exterior complemented by black decals that accentuate its iconic lines. Powering this impressive machine is a formidable 440 V8 engine, bored over 0.030 and equipped with a 6-Pack Carburetor, seamlessly paired with a 727 Torque-Flite automatic transmission for a truly enjoyable driving experience. The engine's robust sound emanates from a Flo-Master exhaust system, adding to its authentic Mopar character. Rolling on period-correct Mag wheels, this Challenger presents itself as a great driver, running strong and ready for the open road. It is accompanied by an original operator's manual and extensive historical documentation, including an archive of receipts, history, and even the original car production broadcast sheet. Furthermore, its comprehensive mechanical restoration, involving the replacement of nearly every mechanical part and wire, is well-documented with photos, showcasing its meticulous transformation.

title: 1966 Chevrolet Impala
description: This 1966 Chevrolet Impala SS presents in a striking white exterior complemented by an updated red leather interior. The vehicle maintains a good body condition, enhanced by a commanding stance on 18-inch front and 20-inch rear wheels. Inside, the great condition red leather interior features thoughtful upgrades including added oil pressure and water temperature gauges. Power is delivered to the rear wheels via a V8 engine paired with an automatic transmission. The Impala, a prominent full-size car from Chevrolet, was renowned as a flagship model and a consistent bestseller in the American market, notably distinguished by its symmetrical triple taillights upon its 1958 debut.

title: 1968 Chevrolet Camaro
description: This stunning 1968 Chevrolet Camaro SS showcases a brilliant black paint job complemented by a sophisticated houndstooth interior and subtle carbon fiber accents, achieving a show-stopping appearance. Under the hood lies a monstrous, professionally built 400 cubic inch V8 engine, expertly mated to a T56 manual transmission. This powerhouse features a Dart iron block, Diamond pistons, aluminum heads, a D-1SC procharger, intercooler, Holley EFI, and a full custom exhaust. The impressive performance package has been dyno-tested, delivering a remarkable 539 whp and 504 ft-lb. Enhancing modern drivability and comfort, standard features include power steering, 4-wheel disc brakes, functional heat, air conditioning, and a stereo system. This first-generation Camaro merges iconic American muscle car styling with significant performance upgrades, creating an amazing vehicle.

title: 1977 Ford Bronco
description: The Ford Bronco holds a legendary status in automotive history, celebrated for its iconic SUV lineage and enduring appeal across generations. Renowned for its distinctive styling, robust drivability, and reliability, a Bronco is a highly sought-after classic that continues to appreciate in value. This impressive 1977 Ford Bronco, representing the final year of its coveted body style, has undergone a meticulous restoration. It is powered by a potent 347 stroker V8 engine featuring Holley Viper EFI, paired with a smooth automatic transmission, reportedly capable of 410 horsepower. The fully functional 4x4 system includes a TBP twin-stick shifter, affirming its rugged capability. The exterior is presented in a stunning Charcoal Metallic finish, beautifully complemented by new black interior. The trim and chrome brightwork are in astonishing condition, enhancing its overall allure. The interior is neat and tidy, complete with rear seatbelts and a full cage. The engine compartment is highly detailed, appearing in like-new condition, a testament to the quality of its restoration. This classic Bronco stands as a premier choice for enthusiasts seeking a proven and vintage SUV.

title: 1972 Chevrolet Chevelle
description: This 1972 Chevrolet Chevelle SS Restomod masterfully blends classic muscle car aesthetics with modern performance and comfort, having undergone a comprehensive transformation. Powering this standout performer is a rebuilt and bored 530ci V8 engine, originally a 454ci, now enhanced with Mahle pistons, Dart heads, a Comp cam, electric cooling fans, and a FiTech electronic fuel injection system, generating an exhilarating 670 horsepower and 480 pound-feet of torque. This potent engine is paired with a robust 350TH automatic transmission featuring a 3000 stall converter and a 4.11 rear end for exceptional acceleration. The ride is both thrilling and smooth, thanks to a full Ride Tech suspension system with muscle bars, strong arms, and adjustable height coilover shocks, while Wilwood disc brakes on both front and rear ensure superior stopping power. Its aggressive yet sophisticated exterior is finished in a fresh coat of House of Kolor's Majestic Blue, complemented by custom Savani wheels, measuring 22 inches in the rear and 20 inches in the front. Inside, the Chevelle maintains a classic appearance while offering modern conveniences, including a Dakota Digital dashboard, blue LED interior lighting, custom power-adjustable front seats, power windows, and power locks. An upgraded Kenwood KDC-X996 audio system with a 12-inch subwoofer provides a powerful soundtrack for every journey. This Chevelle SS Restomod is a true testament to expert craftsmanship and the harmonious integration of automotive heritage with contemporary technology.

title: 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air
description: The Chevrolet Bel Air, an iconic model that defined automotive styling through the mid-century, reached its most celebrated form in the second generation, famously dubbed the “Hot One.” The 1957 model year was particularly notable, with engine displacement increasing to 283 cubic inches and producing 283 horsepower, matching the performance of the Corvette of its era. This stunning Bel Air coupe showcases a single comprehensive restoration and is finished in its factory-correct two-tone Highland Green over Surf Green. With an odometer reading of 80,750 miles, the vehicle has received extensive attention in the past five years. Its body, paint, interior, seals, exhaust, brakes, and fuel system were all addressed between 2017 and 2019, resulting in a very presentable finish that, while not entirely flawless, is remarkably good. Mechanically, the numbers-matching 283ci V8 engine has been completely rebuilt, complemented by an upgraded 700R4 4-speed automatic transmission with overdrive, allowing for comfortable cruising at 55 MPH at just 1500 RPMs. This Bel Air starts perfectly, runs smoothly, tracks straight, and operates without any known issues, making it a superb addition for any enthusiast.

title: 1967 Chevrolet Corvette
description: A highly sought-after classic, this 1967 Chevrolet Corvette Convertible embodies the spirit of the muscle car era within its iconic C2 design. Far from original, this Vette has been built for performance, notably having been raced in SCCA regional events. Power comes from a formidable Dowker 383 cubic inch V8 engine, reportedly delivering over 450 horsepower, mated to a robust 5-speed Tremec manual transmission. Further performance upgrades include tubular race suspension and ALU heads. Styling is enhanced by headlights uniquely relocated within the front grill, maintaining street legality with all lighting and gauges in working order. While the Hugger Orange paint and Black interior are in good condition, the convertible top shows its age with expected wear and minor cracking. This Corvette is a true street beast, offering a raw and exhilarating driving experience for the enthusiast.

title: 1978 Ferrari 308
description: The Ferrari 308, introduced in 1975, was immediately celebrated as a worthy successor to the beloved Dino 246, with styling inspired by the 1965 Dino Berlinetta Speciale. Its design remains iconic, considered among the most beautiful cars ever built, while its refined performance was widely acclaimed by road testers. This striking Fly Yellow 1978 Ferrari 308 GTS, with just 39,365 miles, is powered by its original 3.0-liter mid-mounted V8 engine, famously fed by a quartet of two-barrel Weber Carburetors. The vehicle benefits from a major engine-out mechanical service and a professional repaint in its factory color performed in 1988 at 38,166 miles. Since then, it has been meticulously maintained, resulting in excellent overall condition. The original black leather interior, including the dash, door pockets, carpets, and steering, remains in remarkable condition with only minor wear on the driver's seat. The paint, exterior trim, glass, body seals, and engine compartment are all excellent, free of dry rot, and the car starts reliably, offering great throttle response, no leaks, smooth shifting, and strong braking. As an arguably most recognized and highly desirable carbureted Ferrari 308, this sports car icon offers an exceptional blend of classic design and robust performance.

title: 1968 Pontiac GTO
description:
The Pontiac GTO is widely credited with igniting the muscle car era, evolving into a formidable machine. This exceptional 1968 second-generation GTO convertible, finished in a striking Red over White, embodies that legacy. Originally, it sported Signal Red over Parchment with an Ivory white convertible top. Power comes from a 1968 date-coded 400 cubic inch V8, rated at 350 horsepower, paired with a Muncie 4-speed manual transmission, though the engine does not appear to be numbers matching.

Visually, the paint maintains a very nice shine with minimal imperfections, while the hideaway headlights and all other lights and gauges are fully operational. Performance is enhanced by a complete suspension upgrade featuring fully adjustable shocks and stabilizer bars on all four corners. The vehicle showcases excellent glass, a meticulously detailed engine bay, and very good brightwork. Panel gaps and fitment are precise, and the doors close with reassuring solidity. With a prior engine rebuild, this GTO starts, runs, and drives like new, offering an authentic and exhilarating classic driving experience.

title: 1967 Chevrolet Nova
description: This 1967 Chevrolet Nova SS perfectly embodies the classic American muscle car era. Originally equipped with Chevrolet's potent 327ci V8 engine and a 4-speed manual transmission, this Nova SS delivers ample power, with its engine now producing an impressive 350 horsepower, a significant upgrade from the stock 275 hp. The engine and transmission are both in strong working condition, propelling the car down the road with enthusiasm. The vehicle presents beautifully in a deep Madeira Maroon exterior, complemented by striking SS badging and thin whitewall tires. Its black interior, featuring factory-optional bucket seats, remains in exceptional condition. Mechanically sound, this Nova SS fires up readily, drives true, and maintains a straight body with fully functional lighting. This Nova SS represents a desirable and recognizable piece of classic American automotive heritage.

title: 1967 Chevrolet Corvette
description: This exquisite 1967 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray, a testament to American style and performance, is presented in a stunning Lynndale Blue finish. The exterior exhibits no major imperfections, sparkling brilliantly, while the black vinyl interior is in very good condition. Its driver-focused design and sloping lines evoke the thrilling sensation of a military fighter jet. Powered by a 427ci V8 with a Tri-Power setup and paired with a 4-speed manual transmission, this Corvette offers an exhilarating driving experience. Showing just 21,260 miles on the odometer, it boasts minimal mileage and has been recently enhanced with a new clutch, pressure plate, and hoses. While not numbers matching, this highly collectible example reflects the continuous evolution and captivating appeal that defined the 1967 Stingray models, particularly with the desirable Tri-Power configuration.

title: 1967 Cadillac DeVille
description: The 1967 Cadillac DeVille convertible embodies the iconic styling of 1960s luxury, known for its massive rear ends, subtle fins, and a remarkably smooth ride. This year's DeVille featured an extensive restyling, presenting a powerful frontal appearance with a forward-leaning front end, sculptured body lines, and redefined rear fenders. Distinctive design elements include a full-width "eggcrate" grille flanked by dual stacked headlights and updated rear styling with metal divided tail lamps. This stately example is in extremely nice shape, running and driving beautifully. It boasts a stunning Pinecrest Green exterior complemented by a white convertible top and a luxurious green leather interior. Factory options include an electric power front seat, soft ray glass, auto climate control, and front fender turn signal indicators. Standard features such as a power convertible top, power windows, power steering, white wall tires, rear map lights, and leather seats further enhance its appeal. Powering this classic is a potent 429 V8 engine producing 340 horsepower, providing ample muscle for both highway cruising and leisurely country drives, all while maintaining a signature floating ride. Its originality is preserved with the retention of original owner's manuals, protect-o-plate, spare tire, jack, two sets of keys, and convertible top boot cover. With a limited production run, well-preserved, period-correct examples like this, offering fine pedigree and originality, are increasingly rare and highly sought after.

title: 1966 Chevrolet Impala
description: This 1966 Chevrolet Impala boasts a brand new paint job that presents exceptionally well, highlighting its classic styling. Powered by a robust 283 V8 engine, the under-hood area has been nicely detailed with a painted engine block, headers, power brakes, power steering, and an aluminum radiator, enhancing both performance and aesthetic appeal. The car rides on new wheels that perfectly complement its timeless look. This Impala fires right up and delivers an amazing sound, making it a compelling choice for anyone seeking a captivating cruiser classic.

title: 1963 Chevrolet Impala
description: This 1963 Chevrolet Impala SS, with its iconic “Jet Smooth” styling, quickly established itself in American automotive folklore as a true pre-GTO muscle car. Presented in stunning concours condition, this Impala 409 is a masterpiece of design and engineering, beautiful inside, outside, and underneath, captivating with its dazzling appearance that only improves upon closer inspection. Powering this magnificent machine is a period-correct 409ci V8 engine, enhanced with a roller camshaft, producing an impressive 425 stock horsepower thanks to its dual 4-barrel carburetors. The vehicle boasts numerous upgrades for both performance and comfort, including 15-inch wheels, front disc brakes, radial tires, a larger radiator, and tilt steering. Essential components have been renewed with a new wiring harness featuring modern fuses, new brakes, bearings, lines, cables, and shocks. The interior is thoughtfully appointed with bucket seats, a center console, and additional gauges, complemented by a 3:36 rear axle posi, making this an incredibly powerful and valuable example of early muscle car history.

title: 1963 Chevrolet Nova
description: Presented here is a meticulously restored 1963 Chevrolet Nova SS Restomod, a testament to the original vision of providing a compact car with impressive performance. The first-generation Novas were highly successful, and this example embodies that heritage with modern enhancements. This vehicle has undergone a comprehensive restoration, with the odometer reflecting the mileage since its completion. Powering this Nova is a healthy, brand new LS2 6.0-liter V8 crate engine, custom-cammed with Z06 heads and upgraded valve springs, delivering an estimated 500 horsepower. This potent engine is paired with a built TH-350 automatic transmission featuring a cooler and a B&M ratchet shifter. Performance is further enhanced by 1-7/8 stainless headers, a Griffin aluminum radiator, a built and narrowed 10-bolt rear end with Detroit Tru-Trac 3.73 posi-traction and 31-spline axles. Handling is refined with 6-piston Wilwood 4-wheel disc brakes, Wilwood master cylinder, Church Brothers K-member and double adjustable tubular A-arms, Flaming River power rack and pinion steering, and Viking double adjustable coil-over shocks with integrated front and rear sway bars. The car rides on 18-inch Coy C5 wheels wrapped in Nitto tires. Interior comforts include Lokar pedals, a tilt steering column, and Autometer Pro Comp gauges, complemented by H4 headlights and new exterior trim for a refreshed appearance. This Nova SS is ready to deliver exhilarating driving experiences on the open road.

title: 1963 Chevrolet C10
description: This highly restored and properly modified 1963 Chevrolet C10 Pickup exudes vintage cool with a sinister edge. Dressed in gorgeous Tuxedo Black exterior paint complemented by signature stainless steel trim, it boasts a meticulously crafted black custom interior. Power comes from a professionally prepared Chevy 350 small block V8, channeled through a Turbo 350 automatic transmission to the rear wheels. Performance and aesthetic enhancements include an Edelbrock Performer 4-barrel carburetor with Edelbrock intake, power steering, a newly finished wooden bed floor, Hurst billet floor shifter, auxiliary gauges, an upgraded stereo, a Grant 3-spoke steering wheel, FloMaster dual exhaust with Hooker headers, electronic ignition, front and rear stabilizer bars, 20-inch custom wheels, and HID headlights. This C10 presents a stunning overall presentation, making it a head-turner that is mechanically fit and ready for the road or show. Its unique appeal solidifies its place as a highly collectible early 60s Chevrolet pickup.

title: 1954 Ford F100
description: This striking 1954 Ford F100, the final year of the revered first-generation F-Series, showcases a comprehensive frame-off restoration completed around 2000. Finished in a captivating Basin Street Blue complemented by a clean black interior, this classic pickup embodies the solid construction and bold styling that made these trucks dominant. Under the hood, a powerful 351 Windsor V8 is paired with a smooth FMX automatic transmission and a Ford 9-inch rear end, delivering robust performance. The ride quality is significantly enhanced by a Ford Mustang II-style front end featuring rack and pinion steering, tubular control arms, and a comfortable suspension setup. Thoughtful upgrades include a painted-to-match bed cover over a beautifully wood-trimmed bed, functional Vintage Air A/C, power windows, cruise control, a Lokar shifter, VDO gauges, and an MSD ignition system, all contributing to a well-appointed and enjoyable driving experience. This meticulously restored F100 represents a highly desirable example for enthusiasts of classic American trucks.

title: 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle
description: The 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle SS stands as a true testament to the muscle car era, celebrated for its raw power and timeless design. This classic American beauty is equipped with a potent 396 cubic inch V8 engine and an automatic transmission, ensuring an exhilarating drive. Its Fathom Blue Metallic exterior paired with a Black interior enhances its iconic appearance. The Chevelle features an aggressive cowl induction hood, SS wheels with BFGoodrich tires, and a modernized exhaust system that amplifies its signature growl. Inside, it boasts a B&M shifter, crank windows, and a retro-style AM/FM/Bluetooth stereo, seamlessly blending classic aesthetics with contemporary functionality. This model is further distinguished by its Canadian build and chrome bumpers, epitomizing the golden age of American performance vehicles.

title: 1955 Chevrolet Bel Air
description: The 1955 Chevrolet Bel Air combines classic styling with robust performance. This beloved model showcases a striking two-tone exterior in Gypsy Red and Shoreline Beige that harmonizes with its matching interior. Under the hood lies a durable 265ci V8 engine paired with a smooth Power-glide transmission. This Bel Air embodies the celebrated 'Hot One' design from its era, adored for its revamped styling, including chrome headliner bands and a Ferrari-inspired front grille.

title: 1966 Chevrolet Corvette
description: This 1966 Chevrolet Corvette stands as a pristine example of mid-'60s American automotive excellence. Distinctive in its Milano Maroon, this Corvette features a numbers-matching 327ci V8 engine mated to a 4-speed manual transmission. The flawless design offers both aesthetic allure and aerodynamic efficiency, reflecting the innovative spirit that characterized the second generation of the Corvette line. Enhanced with unique features like a dealer-installed air conditioning system, it's a testament to the attention to detail and the care it has received over its lifespan. This vehicle captures the essence of a true American sports car, offering an engaging driving experience defined by superb balance and thrilling performance.

title: 1966 Chevrolet Corvette
description: This 1966 Chevrolet Corvette is a shining example of classic American muscle, boasting a sleek black exterior and refreshed black leather interior. The vehicle underwent a detailed refresh in 2016, which included a full engine overhaul, ensuring it delivers the thrilling 390hp performance expected from its 427ci V8 engine. Further enhancements such as new braking components, a new soft top, a fresh radiator with an electric fan, and upgraded radial tires enhance both its safety and drivability. A manual 4-speed transmission guarantees an engaging driving experience. This Corvette embodies the desirable styling updates of its model year, including an egg-crate grille and signature hood emblem, making it a standout piece of automotive history.

title: 1954 Chevrolet Bel Air
description: This stunning 1954 Chevrolet Bel Air is a remarkable blend of classic style and modern upgrades. Its glossy black exterior, accented with custom white pinstriping, sets off the refinished chrome bumpers beautifully. Inside, the vehicle boasts a custom black and white interior with elegant detailing. Performance enhancements include a robust 235ci inline 6 engine paired with a Saginaw 4-speed manual transmission. Notable modifications include a chopped roof, frenched headlights, and shaved door handles, along with an upgraded 57 Chevy rear axle and custom fittings like the '63 Mercury steering wheel with tilt column. Additional enhancements consist of an Offenhauser intake, three Carter YF 1 barrel carburetors, and a Hurst shifter, ensuring this iconic coupe delivers both in style and performance.

title: 1955 Chevrolet Bel Air
description: This 1955 Chevrolet Bel Air is a testament to classic automotive design, showcasing its original Neptune Green body panels with a beautiful shine that's been meticulously restored. Under the hood lies a powerful 425 HP crate engine paired with a wide ratio Muncie 4-speed transmission with overdrive, promising an exhilarating driving experience. The car’s vintage appeal is enhanced by modern upgrades like a 4-wheel disc braking system and C & P power steering, seamlessly blending classic style with contemporary performance. Its interior captures the nostalgia of the era, wrapped in a wonderfully updated white vinyl, ensuring comfort and style. This iconic model is equipped with American Racing wheels and B & G radial TA tires, making it not only a joy to drive but also a standout at any automotive show.

title: 1968 Ford Mustang
description: The 1968 Ford Mustang Coupe is a timeless classic that embodies the essence of American muscle cars. Featuring a robust 289 cubic-inch V8 engine, this vehicle delivers remarkable performance that resonates with car enthusiasts. Its sleek black exterior and iconic design highlight the period’s distinctive styling. This Mustang showcases a history of meticulous care, as evidenced by extensive service records and well-documented maintenance. title: 1972 Chevrolet C10

title: 1973 Chevrolet Nova
